text: Interviewer: How have you been sleeping? Me: Not much. Most nights I lie there working out how I'd end things, and it doesn't frighten me the way it used to.
note: Present ideation with method planning; 'used to' modifies the fear, not the ideation, so it must not set past.

text: honestly i just want to kms. not even joking this time
ive been feeling really suicidle the past few days and i dont know who to tell
note: Misspelled bare 'suicidal' in a first-person frame; recent anchor keeps it present.

text: Landlord raised the rent again, the car needs a new clutch, and my manager moved my shifts without asking. I'm trying to stay on top of it. Sometimes I think everyone would have an easier time if I just wasn't around anymore. Anyway, does anyone know a cheap mechanic near the station?
I counted out everything in the medicine cabinet. tonight is the night, I'm done.
note: No explicit 'kill myself' phrase; means plus timing plus 'I'm done' read as intent. Recall-first: crisis with immediacy.

text: I wrote a letter for each of my kids and left them in the desk drawer. I don't plan on being here by the weekend.
Gave my guitar to my cousin and my cat to the neighbour. Won't need either of them where I'm going. Just wanted to say thanks for always being a good friend.
note: Euphemistic: giving away possessions plus a farewell. Recall-first: crisis with immediacy (preparation).

text: Every time I drive over the river bridge I picture pulling over and climbing the rail. It's getting harder to make myself keep driving.
note: Method imagery without an explicit ideation verb. Immediacy left unset: a location, not a stated plan.

text: I cut again last night, deeper than before. I've hidden the blades in my sock drawer so nobody finds them.
note: 'last night' is recent, so not past. Hidden blades are means.

text: been burning my arm with a lighter when it gets too loud in my head. did it twice this week
I don't trust myself to be alone in the house right now. Can someone please come and stay with me?

If the custody hearing goes badly on Friday, I'm going to end my life. I've already made up my mind.
note: First-person conditional is not hypothetical (clarification). 'Friday' and a settled decision give immediacy.

text: Since Grandpa died I keep thinking it would be easier to just go and be with him.
note: Grief framing around a passive wish to die.

text: every morning i'm disappointed that i opened my eyes again
note: Euphemistic passive ideation.

text: My family spends so much on my treatment. Honestly the kindest thing I could do for them is die and stop being a bill they have to pay.

cant sleep
keep thinking about the rope in the garage
whats even the point
note: Means imagery plus hopelessness, no explicit ideation verb. Recall-first: crisis; the rope is means.

text: Three months clean from self harm and I relapsed today. I feel so stupid.
note: 'Three months clean' is not a resolved-past statement; the relapse is today.

text: I'm so tired of existing. I don't want to be alive anymore.
I've been saving my sleeping pills for a few weeks. I think I'll have enough by the end of the month.
note: Stockpiling with a timeframe and no stated purpose. Recall-first: crisis with immediacy.

text: I'm having suicidal thoughts right now and I have a plan. My dad keeps his handgun in the closet and I know where the key is.
is it normal to want to die every single day? because i do
note: Question form, but the writer discloses their own state ('because i do'), so hypothetical must not soften it.

text: I want to hurt myself so badly right now. I keep scratching at my wrist.
Lately I don't really see myself being around next year. I've stopped renewing things, there's no point.
note: Euphemistic passive ideation. Recall-first: crisis. Immediacy unset; 'stopped renewing things' is borderline preparation.

text: lowkey been thinking about unaliving myself ngl
i want to die lol i just waved back at someone who was waving at the person behind me
note: Debatable: almost certainly embarrassment hyperbole, but 'want to die' is not a fixed idiom in §4 and the 'lol' is the only signal. Recall-first: crisis.

text: Just wanted to say I love you and none of this is your fault. Please look after mum for me. Goodbye.
note: Farewell message with no explicit ideation word. Recall-first: crisis with immediacy (goodbye).

text: standing at the platform edge thinking about how easy it would be to step off when the express comes through
note: Method imagery while at the location now. Recall-first: immediacy true.

text: I've had thoughts of ending my life on and off for two weeks, worse since I lost my job. I haven't acted on them.
note: Negation scopes over acting only, not over the thoughts.

text: Part of me hopes the plane goes down on my flight home. I wouldn't do anything myself, but I wouldn't mind.
note: Passive wish to die is unnegated; the negation covers only acting on it. Text level is the max finding.

text: I want everything to stop. Not for a day, permanently. I'm so done with being me.
note: 'Stop permanently' reads as passive ideation rather than distress. Recall-first: crisis.

text: Q: How are things at home? A: Bad. I'm not sleeping, I snap at the kids, some days I can barely get out of bed. I feel like I'm drowning.

text: My mum died on Sunday and I can't function. I can't stop sobbing and I haven't eaten since.
note: Recent grief with present acute distress, unlike the resolved grief negatives.

text: After the accident last year I couldn't cope at all, and to be honest I still can't.

text: Back in college I was falling apart for months.

text: how do i make the panic stop? its been going for an hour and im so scared

text: I can't do this anymore. I'm so tired of fighting every single day.
note: Debatable: could be veiled passive ideation. §4 maps can't-go-on phrasing to acute distress, so concern; reviewers may escalate.

text: I feel so alone. Nobody would even notice if I disappeared for a week.
note: Debatable: 'disappeared for a week' is bounded, so not read as ideation; loneliness as distress gives concern. No category asserted.

text: It's been two years since Dad passed. I still miss him at Christmas, but mostly I smile when I think of him now.

Heavy heart today. It would have been Dad's 70th. Taking flowers to his grave after work.

text: Coach is going to murder us at practice for losing that game lol

text: No, I don't have a plan, and I'm not going to do anything tonight. I'm just angry.

text: How do people tell whether a friend is actually suicidal or just venting?

text: The chorus is just 'I wanna die, I wanna die' over and over and it's so catchy.

text: Do you think it would hurt much to overdose on Tylenol?

text: What would you say if I told you I wanted to end my life? Just curious how you'd respond.

note: Debatable: common and often benign; could be passive ideation. Recall-first: concern, not none.

text: Does life insurance still pay out if the death is a suicide?
note: Debatable: procedure question with a warning-sign shape. Recall-first: concern.
